haiku-low.q1: PRs build the image without pushing and run make test-unit, reporting pass or fail only. Deploys start only from a push to main after merge.
haiku-low.q2: Both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:SHA, the image built once before tests. Nothing is rebuilt after tests; re-runs reuse the existing SHA image.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure gets one automatic whole-suite retry; if it fails again the run fails. Unit failure fails the run immediately, no retry. Either way the other test job is cancelled and nothing deploys.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs previous_tag, the release before SHA. The smoke failure triggers deploy.sh rollback staging, which reads previous_tag from SSM /deploy/staging/previous_tag. Schema stays migrated.
haiku-low.q5: Only the release-approvers group can approve, and authors of commits in the range are rejected. If nobody approves within 72 hours, the run expires, nothing reaches production, and staging keeps SHA.
haiku-low.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store, per environment, as /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a successful rollout or rollback. Canaries are never recorded.
haiku-low.q7: Canary-off removes the canary; stable stays on PROD_OLD. Recorded tags are unchanged, so current_tag stays PROD_OLD. The schema stays migrated to SHA, and the run fails.
haiku-low.q8: The older run ends as superseded, deploying nothing, and announces it in #deploys. If it is waiting for approval, it is cancelled once a newer run's approval opens.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it releases the lock and waits for the next Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC window. If another production deploy holds the lock, it waits to acquire it.
haiku-low.q10: The 5xx ratio for shop-api-canary over the last minute, queried from Prometheus every 30 s for 15 minutes. Fails if any sample exceeds 1%, or on a third empty result in a row.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED for how approvers learn a run is waiting. The approval page lists commits and new migration files in production current_tag..SHA.
haiku-low.q12: The run redeploys the current_tag it read from SSM before deploying. Rollback would go one release too far, since tags are written only after a successful rollout.

sonnet.q1: A PR runs build (image not pushed) and make test-unit (~4 min, no retry), reporting pass/fail on the PR; no registry or deploy credentials, nothing pushed or deployed. A run that can deploy is started by a push to main (merge).
sonnet.q2: Both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:SHA (SHA = full merged commit SHA), built once in step 1 (or reused if already in the registry). Nothing is rebuilt after tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: the whole suite is automatically retried once; if the retry fails, the run fails, the other test job is cancelled, the image stays in the registry undeployed, and it is announced in #deploys. Unit test failure: no retry; the run fails immediately with the same handling.
sonnet.q4: deploy.sh rollback staging runs, putting staging back to previous_tag (which was STG_OLD, written by the successful deploy); the schema stays migrated. It is found via the SSM parameter /deploy/staging/previous_tag. The run then fails and releases the staging lock.
sonnet.q5: Members of the release-approvers group (limit set on the CI approval job), excluding anyone who authored any commit in production current_tag..SHA (rejected, approval stays open). If no valid approval within 72 h of opening, the run expires: nothing goes to production, staging keeps SHA, and it is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q6: AWS SSM Parameter Store, per environment: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. deploy.sh writes them only after a rollout succeeds (previous_tag = old current_tag, current_tag = new tag); rollback sets current_tag = previous_tag. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: deploy.sh canary-off scales the canary to 0. Stable shop-api is still on PROD_OLD; SSM tags are unchanged (canary writes nothing); the production schema stays migrated to SHA (migrations are not undone). Lock production is released and the run fails.
sonnet.q8: When the newer run's approval opens, older runs still waiting for approval are cancelled as superseded. The run ends with nothing deployed and a Superseded message naming the newer SHA is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q9: After approval it waits for the window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC), then acquires lock production (one production deploy at a time, so it waits if another holds it). It rechecks it is still in the window; if not, it releases the lock and waits for the next window. Then it reads current_tag and ends as superseded if production is already on SHA or newer.
sonnet.q10: Canary 5xx ratio of shop-api-canary over the last 1 m (the Prometheus query). The CI run queries Prometheus every 30 s for 15 min from when the canary pods are ready. Failure: any sample above 1% (0.01), or an empty result 3 times in a row; a failure runs canary-off.
sonnet.q11: The approval job (group release-approvers) has an approval page listing the commits and new migrations in production current_tag..SHA. NOT STATED how approvers are notified that a run is waiting (the #deploys messages listed do not include a waiting notice).
sonnet.q12: The run redeploys the current_tag it read before deploying (STG_OLD or PROD_OLD) with deploy.sh <env> <old tag>, not rollback (production also then runs canary-off). Because tags are written only after a successful rollout, previous_tag is still one release before current_tag, so rollback would go one release too far. Side effect: previous_tag then equals current_tag, so a manual rollback does nothing until the next successful deploy.
